references.text: Pharaoh had previously warned Moses not to appear before him again, but after the tenth plague he desperately calls for Moses during the night.
The Lord had predicted that Pharaoh would drive the Israelites out of Egypt after the final plague.
The tenth plague, the death of the firstborn, which led to Pharaoh calling for Moses and Aaron during the night.
God's promise to Moses that the people would serve Him on the mountain after their deliverance from Egypt.
Moses and Aaron's initial demand to Pharaoh to let the people go to serve the Lord.
The repeated demand to let the people go to serve the Lord.
Egypt was glad when the Israelites left, for fear had fallen upon them because of the plagues.
Stephen's speech refers to Moses leading the people out of Egypt with signs and wonders.
The Letter to the Hebrews mentions Passover and the blood that protected the firstborn, which led to their deliverance.
Both verses focus on the critical moment when the 'break camp' command is given to set the exodus in motion.
The source verse is the historical fulfillment of the command given in the candidate's verse to let the people go to serve God.
